inputs.text: ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.

fields.description: Fog warning: thick fog may cut visibility to zero at times across western regions of the UAE, from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Source: National Center for Meteorology.
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions
fields.instruction: Drive with extreme caution. Keep a safe distance and follow reduced speed limits in fog. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so none were excluded.
The 'Abu Dhabi' dateline is where the news story was filed, not a stated fog area, so it is not used as a location.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I chose severity Moderate and certainty Likely because NCM describes 'potential' fog, though possible zero visibility could justify Severe. NCM says 'several western regions' without naming them, so please confirm the operator's demo zone matches that area.

thick fog may cut visibility to zero at times across western regions of the UAE

objections.fix: Reword to match the bulletin, for example: 'Fog may form and visibility may drop to zero at times across several western regions of the UAE, from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb.' Use 'several western regions' in the headline too.
objections.issue: The place wording is broader than the bulletin. The NCM bulletin covers 'several western regions of the UAE'. The alert says 'across western regions', and the description calls the fog 'thick', which implies a wider and firmer hazard than the bulletin's 'potential fog formation'. The bulletin mentions thick fog only in its safety advice, as 'areas experiencing thick fog'.

payload.summary: Hazard, timing (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb), source, Moderate severity and Likely certainty all match the NCM bulletin. One minor non-blocking issue: the alert widens the bulletin's 'several western regions' to all western regions and presents the fog as certain to be thick, when the bulletin speaks of potential fog formation.

no_basis.concern: The registered sender is a demo stand-in ('Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)'). It is not one of the entities named as authorised to send warnings, such as NCEMA. Even so, it would be issuing an Actual alert on a live console for a real event. People should confirm that a demo issuer identity is meant to send live Actual alerts.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause that bars a demo or stand-in sender from issuing Actual alerts in a live environment. UAE-PORTAL-EWS#0027 lists the authorised entities, but the register and the sender match, and no shown clause addresses demo identities, so I am not making this an objection.

The alert's area matches the area requested for this event: the description is the same and the codes are DEMO-ZONE AUH-WEST. objections.fix: Add a short protective action in both English and Arabic, placed right after the hazard so it falls on the first page. For example: 'Fog warning: zero visibility possible in western UAE. Avoid travel; if driving, slow down, use low beams, keep distance.' Then give the times and source. In Arabic, keep the hazard and action within the first 41-character page as far as possible, e.g. 'ضباب كثيف: تجنب القيادة، وإن اضطررت فخفف السرعة' followed by details. Keep each language at 15 pages or fewer.
objections.issue: No protective action appears anywhere in either language, so the first page carries the hazard but not the action. The alert only describes the fog and its timing, and never says what people should do (for example, avoid unnecessary travel, drive slowly with low-beam lights, keep a safe distance). The CAP guidance expects people to act on the guidance the alert provides.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Encoding is correct: English is GSM-7, and Arabic is UCS-2 as 3GPP requires. Both are within the 15-page maximum (3 and 6 pages). However, neither language gives any protective action, on the first page or anywhere else. The text states the hazard, area, time and source but never tells people what to do. The drafter can fix this.

payload.summary: The Arabic matches the English in meaning across all three fields. The headline carries the same hazard, zero visibility and western regions. The description has the same times and dates: 21:30 Tuesday 17 February until 10:00 Wednesday 18 February. It names the same area (western regions of the UAE), the same 'at times' qualifier and the same source (National Center for Meteorology). The instruction gives the same protective actions: drive with extreme caution, keep a safe distance and follow reduced speed limits in fog. The URL is identical. I found no difference in numbers, times, places, hazard or protective action. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named person who reads Arabic must still review and sign it off before sending; this check does not replace that.

fields.description: Fog may form in several western regions of the UAE. Drivers: take extreme care, keep a safe distance, obey modified speed limits. Visibility may drop to zero at times from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Source: NCM. More: alerts.example.ae
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in several western regions of the UAE
fields.instruction: If you drive, take extreme care, follow traffic safety guidelines and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Strictly obey modified speed limits, especially in areas with thick fog.
left_out: The network reviewer's suggested actions 'avoid travel' and 'use low beams' were left out. The NCM bulletin does not include them, so the instruction uses only the bulletin's advice: extreme caution, traffic safety guidelines, safe distance, modified speed limits.

No Arabic text is included because this draft is English only. The network reviewer's Arabic example starts with 'ضباب كثيف' (thick fog), which conflicts with the Met reviewer's correction. Any Arabic version should not lead with 'thick fog'.
'Thick' is not used as a description of the hazard. It appears only in the instruction, matching the bulletin's own safety advice ('areas experiencing thick fog').
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set certainty to Likely because NCM says visibility is 'expected to deteriorate', even though fog formation is called 'potential'. Severity is Moderate despite possible zero visibility; please confirm both. The operator's 'Western region (demo zone)' area should be checked against the bulletin's 'several western regions of the UAE', which names no specific places.

payload.summary: The sender is in the issuer register with all areas and categories. The alert area exactly matches the area requested for event uae-fog-2026-02-17. Status 'Actual' with msgType 'Alert' fits a real event on the live console, and references are correctly empty for a first alert. no_basis.concern: At 41 UCS-2 characters a page, the Arabic first page reads roughly 'قد يتشكل الضباب في عدة مناطق غربية من الإم…'. It carries the hazard (fog) but not the action (توخوا الحذر الشديد…), which falls on page 2. The time window, from 21:30 tonight, also falls on later pages in both languages. The drafter could shorten the Arabic opening so the hazard and the action both fit in the first 41 characters, for example 'ضباب كثيف: قللوا السرعة وتوخوا الحذر…'.
no_basis.searched_for: A TDRA or 3GPP clause requiring the first cell broadcast page to carry the hazard and the protective action. The search 'cell broadcast first page hazard action' returned no such requirement. TS 23.041 and TS FS 001 cover only paging, encoding and handset display.

The English first page carries both the hazard (fog) and the driver action. The Arabic first page, about 41 characters, carries only the hazard. I have logged that under no_basis because no clause shown to me supports objecting to it.
